seo.title: Mastercard: generative AI fraud detection (Decision Intelligence Pro) - +20% detection (2024)
seo.meta_description: Decision Intelligence Pro scores each transaction in less than 50 ms. Mastercard modeling: +20% fraud detection on average, -85% false positives.
seo.resume_citable: In 2024, Mastercard launched Decision Intelligence Pro, a generative model that scores each transaction in less than 50 ms; its internal modeling reports +20% fraud detection on average (up to +300%) and more than 85% fewer false positives.

faq.q: How does Decision Intelligence Pro work?
faq.a: The generative model assesses the relationships between the entities around a transaction, scans a trillion data points and refines a risk score in less than 50 milliseconds, passed to the issuing bank.
According to its initial modeling, the improvement raises the fraud detection rate by 20% on average, up to 300% in some cases, and reduces false positives by more than 85%.

objectif_business: Help issuing banks distinguish legitimate transactions from fraudulent ones in real time, to block more fraud while reducing false declines that degrade experience and lose revenue.
description: Decision Intelligence assigns a risk score to each transaction on the network. In February 2024, Mastercard launched Decision Intelligence Pro, a version that relies on a generative model to assess the relationships between the entities around a transaction (merchant, terminal, behavior). The model scans a trillion data points to predict whether a transaction is likely authentic, and refines the Decision Intelligence score in less than 50 milliseconds. According to Mastercard's initial modeling, the improvement raises the fraud detection rate by 20% on average, up to 300% in some cases, and reduces false positives by more than 85%.
points_cles: Real-time fraud risk scoring on every transaction on the network.
Decision Intelligence Pro, transformer-type generative model, score refined in under 50 ms.
+20% detection on average (up to +300%), false positives reduced by more than 85%.
Evidence B, confirmed status: Mastercard internal modeling, picked up by CNBC and PYMNTS.

resultats.metrique: Improvement in the fraud detection rate, up to +300% in some cases (initial modeling)
Reduction in false positives (Mastercard internal analysis)
Scoring speed, scan of 1 trillion data points

niveau_preuve.justification: Figures from Mastercard's official press release (internal analysis and modeling, interested source) and picked up by name by CNBC and PYMNTS. These are initial modeling results, not audited financial KPIs; the +20% and +300% are presented by Mastercard as projections, which the record preserves.

stack_technique.detail: real-time risk scoring on every transaction on the network, passed to issuing banks at authorization
transformer-type generative model (launched in February 2024) that assesses the relationships between entities (merchant, terminal, behavior) and refines the score in less than 50 ms
a trillion data points scanned; the confirmed-fraud labels serve for retraining
consumes the score in the authorization rules; the final decision stays with the issuer, supervisable and contestable (GDPR, AI Act)

fonctionnement_operationnel.cadence: Real time, on every transaction on the network, with periodic retraining of the models.
fonctionnement_operationnel.opere_par: Mastercard's cyber and intelligence team on the network side; risk teams of issuing banks on the final decision side.
fonctionnement_operationnel.signal_pilote: Transaction behavior and the relationships between entities (merchant, terminal, history). If the confirmed-fraud label signal degrades, the model drifts and accuracy drops.

etapes.detail: A transaction arrives for authorization on the Mastercard network.
The model assesses the relationships between entities and scans the context to assign a risk score in less than 50 ms.
Decision Intelligence Pro refines the overall score passed to the bank.
The issuing bank approves or declines the transaction based on the score and its own rules.

prerequis_data: History of confirmed fraud for learning
Relational data between entities (merchant, terminal, device)
prerequis_orga: Ability to integrate an external score into the authorization decision engine
Risk team to calibrate the thresholds
stack_possible: custom model if internal volume and data are sufficient
replication.equipe: 2-3 risk/fraud analysts + 1-2 payment devs for the integration + compliance for the automated decision

playbook.action: Frame with the network the activation of the score on the relevant card portfolio
playbook.livrable: Activation scope + access to the score in the authorization flow

playbook.action: Plug the score into the decision engine, first in observation mode without blocking
playbook.livrable: Score consumed in production, logged on real traffic

playbook.action: Calibrate the thresholds by segment with the risk team, on history and observed traffic
playbook.livrable: Tested threshold matrix, trade-off between fraud detected and false declines

playbook.action: Move to decision mode on a pilot segment and compare against a control period
playbook.livrable: Measurement of detection rate, false positives and approval rate

playbook.action: Generalize to the portfolio and close the retraining loop with confirmed-fraud labels
playbook.livrable: Detection, false-positive and approval dashboard tracked continuously

replication.premiere_etape: For an issuer: plug the existing network score into the authorization rules and measure the effect on false declines and fraud.

statut_vivant.note: Decision Intelligence is a core Mastercard product. The Pro version launched in 2024 is confirmed active by a 2026 Mastercard publication on the savings generated by anti-fraud AI for banks.

transposable_ue.note: Mastercard operates this scoring on its network, including in the EU. Real-time fraud scoring processes transaction data; under the GDPR and AI Act, the automated decline decision must remain supervisable and contestable by the issuing bank.
